sections.title: Looking and Making
sections.description:
This class introduces students to the fundamentals of Visual Studies and Fine Arts. A hybrid studio and seminar, students will consider foundational images across cultures and time, how they were made and interpreted, and how to respond to these histories through observation and analysis as well as a variety of visual and material approaches. Students will experiment with historic and contemporary image-making technologies including digital and analog photographic practices, printmaking and mixed media, and will also learn about presentation strategies, exhibition and curation. Students will visit art shows and archives on and off campus.
Students will come away with an understanding of how power, politics, identity and belief are shaped and shown through images, making and the act of looking. They will also gain awareness about the materiality of the seen: what physical matter constitutes the media that we look at, and why this matters. Students will grow in their sense of their own visual language, proclivities for looking and making, and ability to articulate about the visual world.
Course content draws from visual studies, art history and theory, cinema and media studies, anthropology and philosophy. Methodologies of slow looking and visual analysis, semiotic interpretation and ekphrasis will be employed. There will 3-4 creative projects with affi liated reading and writing components, and dialogue-centered critique and feedback. This seminar serves as an excellent foundation for those interested in visual studies, art, design, art history, media or communications fi elds.
